paper.abstract_en: After a historical introduction, the most important classical and quantum entropies are introduced as constructions in classical and quantum probability theory. Classical entropies are studied from large deviation theory, including theorems of Sanov, Cramér, Gärtner-Ellis, and Varadhan, and are illustrated in some applications to both Boltzmannian and Gibbsian statistical physics. Quantum entropies superficially connect to classical entropies at the formula level, but more deeply do so via the crucial role of entropy in statistical hypothesis testing. The classical (relative) Kullback-Leibler entropy, its quantum counterpart introduced by Umegaki, as well as their deformations proposed by Renyi all fit naturally in this context. Quantum entropy faces the new problem of defining and computing the relative entropy of a pair of states on a subsystem, here formalized as a von Neumann algebra. This requires modular (aka Tomita-Takesaki) theory, which provides the framework for the relative quantum entropies introduced by Araki and Uhlmann (these encompass both the Kullback-Leibler and Umegaki entropies as special cases). To (re)define and compute these entropies in terms of density operators and traces, further constructions are needed, namely Haagerup's noncommutative L^p spaces. Von Neumann algebras also provide the setting for the Connes-Stormer-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy, which is a quantum version of the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy in dynamical systems and ergodic theory, to which we also provide an introduction. This course was originally inspired by, and should be relevant to, black hole thermodynamics, although we discuss neither this application nor the second law. The course tries to be both mathematically rigorous and interesting to theoretical physicists. Prerequisites are undergraduate probability theory, functional analysis, and quantum theory.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文系统介绍了经典与量子熵的数学基础，并明确提及与黑洞热力学的相关性，具备高度的理论深度和教学价值。
decision.abstract_zh: 在历史性介绍之后，最重要的经典和量子熵被作为经典和量子概率论中的构造而引入。经典熵从大偏差理论的角度进行研究，包括Sanov、Cramér、Gärtner-Ellis和Varadhan定理，并在玻尔兹曼和吉布斯统计物理的一些应用中加以说明。量子熵在公式层面上表面上与经典熵相关，但更深入地通过熵在统计假设检验中的关键作用而相关。经典的（相对）Kullback-Leibler熵、由Umegaki引入的量子对应物，以及由Renyi提出的它们的变形，都自然地适合这个背景。量子熵面临定义和计算子系统上一对状态的相对熵的新问题，这里将其形式化为冯·诺依曼代数。这需要模（即Tomita-Takesaki）理论，它为Araki和Uhlmann引入的相对量子熵提供了框架（这些熵包含Kullback-Leibler和Umegaki熵作为特殊情况）。为了用密度算子和迹来（重新）定义和计算这些熵，需要进一步的构造，即Haagerup的非交换L^p空间。冯·诺依曼代数也为Connes-Stormer-Narnhofer-Thirring熵提供了背景，它是动力系统和遍历理论中Kolmogorov-Sinai熵的量子版本，我们也对此进行了介绍。本课程最初受到黑洞热力学的启发，并且应该与黑洞热力学相关，尽管我们既不讨论这一应用也不讨论第二定律。本课程力求既数学严谨又能引起理论物理学家的兴趣。先修课程是本科概率论、泛函分析和量子理论。
